I try to keep my thoughts on the present, mostly. \n\nI hope it doesn't sound like I didn't care about him! I did, very much. I just... I try to be strong about it. Is that... is that a normal way to handle things? Does that sound like I'm coping alright?\n\nDoctor: Do you think staying constantly busy and active helps keep your mind off thoughts or feelings about your husband's death?\n\nPatient: Oh, um... well, I suppose you could say that. I like to be useful, you know? \n\nMost days I just sort of... well, I move from the garden, and then maybe over to the senior center, and then there are always errands for the church, and then I come home and sort through papers... all without really taking a breath. I try so hard to just relax like everyone else does, but it's very difficult. \n\nDoes that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too... difficult or anxious. I really try not to let myself wallow, you know? I want to be strong. \n\nIt's really just... it's just this physical feeling. Like my legs just need to get up and go, and my hands need to be doing something. It's not that I'm sitting there crying or feeling sorry for myself, I promise. It's just... I just feel so fidgety and restless, like a motor is running inside me that I can't turn off. \n\nI hope that doesn't sound like I'm hiding my feelings or anything. I just... I don't feel sad when I sit still, I just feel like I absolutely have to move. Is that alright? Does that make sense to you?\n\nDoctor: \n\nPatient: Doctor: I understand.
